clue.text: Catcher accepts unfinished poem: don't talk to the messenger

indicators.note: a catcher that accepts something takes it inside, so the poem goes into the trap

parts.note: a trap is a device for catching

indicators.note: the poem is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem
hist is an old interjection calling for silence

explanation.surface: Someone told to hush while a poem is half-written and a catcher stands by, as the messenger arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the poem's last letter, and 'accepts' puts what remains inside the catcher after its first letter. Hist is an archaic call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraph operator sends and receives messages, so is a kind of messenger.

clue.text: Sunburn for man like the ground to a wheel?

definitions.text: like the ground to a wheel?

parts.note: a tan is skin browned by the sun
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A sunburnt man is somehow compared with how a wheel meets the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel touches flat ground at a single point, just as a straight line touches a circle in geometry.

clue.text: Last year's leaders keep carnivore on spec

indicators.note: the two opening letters hold the animal between them
the leaders of the two words are their opening letters

parts.note: the otter is a meat-eating (strictly fish-eating) mammal

explanation.surface: Last year's top people take on a predator speculatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes L and Y from 'Last year's'; 'keep' puts OTTER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Spec is short for speculation, a gamble, and a lottery is a matter of pure chance.

clue.text: Fellow with divisions in road, reportedly — he gets burnt

parts.note: guy is slang for a man

indicators.note: signals that the word for divisions in a road is heard rather than seen

parts.note: forks are places where a road splits

explanation.surface: A man somewhere among the branching roads is going to be set on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes plotted to blow up Parliament in 1605; on 5 November Britons burn his effigy on bonfires.
explanation.definitionFit: The effigy of the Gunpowder Plot conspirator is burnt each Bonfire Night, so he is the one burnt.

clue.text: Submarine detector sounds like small boy

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison

indicators.note: a small version of the name is one cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Dick is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A device for finding submarines is said to sound like a little lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic was the British name for sonar, the echo-sounding system used to locate submarines underwater.

clue.text: Beast gets hot on Dutch dam

annotationWithheld.why: Beast gets hot on Dutch dam (7): the blog parses H + AMSTER(dam), but no clue word signals removing DAM from AMSTERDAM; 'dam' would both name the letters and signal their removal
annotationWithheld.clue: Beast gets hot on Dutch dam

clue.text: Brock's home was first to be colonised

parts.note: brock is an old name for a badger, whose burrow is a sett
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A badger's burrow was the first place to be occupied by settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that has been colonised has had people move in and make homes there.

clue.text: Kit's here, stupid! The man's a journalist

parts.note: clot is British slang for a fool
he's is short for he is
the press stands for journalism and those who practise it

explanation.surface: Someone is called stupid for asking where the clothes are, and told the man works for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A clothes-press is a wardrobe or cupboard for clothes, not a trouser press.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-press is a cupboard in which one's garments, or kit, are kept.

clue.text: Little boy sees good solver's much extended

parts.note: Len is a short form of Leonard
the clue addresses the solver as you, and thy is old English for your

explanation.surface: A small boy finds that a good solver's work has gone on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lengthy has been drawn out at great length, i.e. much extended.

clue.text: Popular protest leads to convulsion

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A protest ends up causing a fit among the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of or for the common people, so popular in the sense of the populace.

clue.text: Rule about little room at first needing scrubbing

indicators.note: the rule goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a canon is a rule or law
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
I is the Roman numeral one, i.e. first

explanation.surface: A rule about a small room comes first, before any cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubbing a plan or booking means calling it off, which is a cancellation.

clue.text: She doesn't say what there is

definitions.text: She doesn't say what there is

parts.words: She doesn't say what there is
parts.note: a woman's name which, broken after its fifth letter, is the start of a sentence announcing something, cut off before the thing itself is named

explanation.surface: A woman who never tells you what is actually there.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the name as three words of speech and the clue's joke appears: she starts to point something out and never finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, read as a phrase, starts to announce something and stops short.

clue.text: Pet for boy from Barcelona

parts.note: a cat is a common pet
Alan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pet is bought for a boy who comes from Barcelona.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the capital of Catalonia, so a native of it is a Catalonian.

clue.text: Fish has left woodwork at gate

indicators.note: the fish leaves, so its letters are removed from the woodwork

parts.note: carpentry is the craft of working wood
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish has escaped from some woodwork at a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is a way in, such as a gate or door.

clue.text: Get in line, say, for game across the Thames

indicators.note: signals that the word for getting in line is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to queue is to wait in line
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone told to line up for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Bridge crosses the Thames in west London, by Kew Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Kew Bridge is one of the road bridges spanning the Thames in London.

clue.text: Successfully? It's not the end of the world

definitions.text: It's not the end of the world
definitions.meaning: T. S. Eliot's The Hollow Men ends

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means with great success, and Eliot says the world ends otherwise than this.

clue.text: Go to a museum, perhaps, even if it's free?

definitions.text: Go to a museum, perhaps, even if it's free?

parts.words: Go to a museum, perhaps, even if it's free?
parts.note: visiting a free museum costs nothing, yet the idiom for calling in still talks of paying

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to call on a place or person, though nothing is actually paid.

clue.text: Language of heart-throb after rise of homework

indicators.note: the heart-throb comes after the other piece
in a down clue a rise reads upwards, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's home
a dish is an attractive person

explanation.surface: The language of a pin-up appears after a rise in homework.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY (do-it-yourself) is home improvement work, which makes it 'homework'; 'rise of' turns it to YID in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is the language of Ashkenazi Jews, based on German with Hebrew elements.

clue.text: Sticky 6 from Liverpool didn't finish

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Scouse means from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A sticky number six from Liverpool failed to complete the course.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a reference to 6-down but is just the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscous liquid is thick and syrupy, so sticky.

clue.text: Little one left in tower

parts.note: a babe is a baby

explanation.surface: A small child left inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of Babel is the Bible tower whose builders were confounded by many languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Babel is the tower in Genesis built to reach heaven.

clue.text: A few lines — got some between the teeth

parts.note: a bit is the bar placed in a horse's mouth, between its teeth
part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Getting a mouthful of something stuck in the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link word; the pieces join in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small acting role with only a few lines to speak.

clue.text: Three bachelors, real weird, that will talk too much

indicators.note: weird suggests letters thrown into an odd order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree, so three of them make BBB

explanation.surface: Three unmarried men, really strange, who just can't stop chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A blabber is one who blabs, chattering and giving away secrets.

clue.text: Slough disposal is after its first during reversion of Indian groom

indicators.note: after here means following in sequence, so the short word is placed at the end of what has been built
the first letter sits inside the reversed groom
reversion means turning back, so the groom's word is read backwards

parts.note: a syce is a groom in India

indicators.note: only the opening letter of disposal is used

explanation.surface: Some disposal business in Slough follows a turnaround by an Indian stable lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversion of' turns the groom backwards, giving ECYS, and 'during' puts D inside it. Slough is also the English town near London, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecdysis is the moulting of an outer skin, as when a snake sloughs.

clue.text: Capital seat accommodating setter

indicators.note: the seat makes room for the setter inside it

parts.note: a sofa is a seat
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A capital seat with room for the puzzle's author.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Draw a model for area

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a model in place of an area.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw in, as a magnet draws iron.

clue.text: Philosopher abandoning both extremes for very noisy derivative

indicators.note: the alphabet's two extremes, Z and A, are dropped and replaced

parts.note: Spinoza was a Dutch philosopher
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A thinker gives up his extreme views in favour of something loud and derivative.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes are those of the alphabet, A and Z, which here happen to end Spinoza.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-off is a product derived from something else, so a derivative.

clue.text: Change round in the morning: phone company books men to deride innocent victim

indicators.note: the word for change goes round all the other pieces

parts.note: to alter is to change
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
BT is British Telecom
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
hes are males, a plural of he
to laugh at is to deride

explanation.surface: An early-morning switch as a phone company books staff to mock a helpless victim.
explanation.walkthrough: The change word is split after its second letter to hold the five inner pieces. HES, as a plural of he meaning males, is a liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone led unknowingly to their ruin, an innocent victim.
